name: security-ios-app-group-storage-review
intent: iOS App Group container authority across app and extension identities
artifacts: Signed entitlements, app/extension provisioning, group container paths and file/key access lifecycle.
trace: Trace which signed components can reach shared data and whether lower-trust extension input changes another component protected state.
experiment: Use owned signed test targets and synthetic shared data; compare intended extension exchange with an out-of-policy action/resource selection.
disproof: A shared group identifier is not proof that an unrelated app can access it; entitlement enforcement remains essential.
repair: Constrain shared data and per-operation authority within entitled components, preserving legitimate extensions.
branch_decisions: Use signed entitlements of each app/extension and the actual shared container identifier. App Group sharing is intentional among authorized members; the boundary may instead be account switching or an untrusted extension capability. A directory name seen in source is not proof of installed access or cross-team container entitlement.
operational_method: Separate App Group file-container access from Keychain access-group entitlements; sharing one does not imply the other. Retain signed entitlements, the actual container API/path, file protection class and extension/application identity. Compare a synthetic account switch or extension read against the declared audience/lifecycle. Merely showing that authorized group members share a container is expected behavior, not cross-team privilege.
